summary: Mark Twain National Forest tower beside Missouri 76, built by Camp F-20 enrollees in December 1935; still standing but no longer active, per a visitor guide.

facts.design: 100-foot steel tower with a lookout cupola
facts.status_note: Still standing but no longer active, per a visitor guide. No source says whether it can be climbed.
facts.agency: Mark Twain National Forest (U.S. Forest Service)

access.note: Just off MO 76 in national forest land; the visitor guide gives directions. No source says whether the tower itself may be climbed today.

visit.trail_note: About 1.2 miles west of MO Hwy 39 on MO Hwy 76, between Shell Knob and Cassville.

events.note: Under construction by enrollees of Camp F-20 at Shell Knob in December 1935; the Cassville Republican called it the first 100-foot steel tower on the Table Rock Unit. A Joplin paper reported it nearing completion on December 15. Completion is expected, not documented, in these sources.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: OpenStreetMap, with a GNIS-linked tag, spells the tower Lahmer Fire Lookout Tower. The Central US Lookouts register page, the Explore the Ozarks visitor guide and Wikipedia's community article spell it Lohmer, the same as the community. The story uses Lohmer and notes the map spelling.

sources.title: Mark Twain National Forest - Discover History

notes_for_editor: Name: the brief says Lahmer, from OpenStreetMap; local sources say Lohmer. GNIS may use Lahmer too, which I could not check, so the name is left for the editor to decide. Wikipedia's community coordinates sit about 50 m from the record point. The 1935 elevation figure in the central page (1569 ft, about 478 m) differs slightly from OSM's 479 m; not changed. A 1940 Joplin Globe item on the same page mentions a Lomersburg fire tower six miles east of town; it does not name Lohmer, so it is not used. The 1935 'visitors may climb' notice is historical and not used. The visitor guide is undated. The record's height_m was null; the 100 ft figure comes from 1935 reporting.
